subScores.label: Team
subScores.rationale: Strong founder-market fit in voice AI and deep technical depth from Stanford PhDs. However, prior startup/exit history is not clearly documented, preventing a higher score.

subScores.label: Defensibility
subScores.rationale: Proprietary voice recognition technology provides some defensibility, but the platform is horizontal and switching costs are moderate. Not a thin LLM wrapper, but dependence on broad ecosystem limits moat.

subScores.label: Product
subScores.rationale: Product is a voice AI platform, not a vertical-specific end-to-end agent. Self-serve onboarding via APIs is possible, but the one-liner is clear. Lacks the AI-native agent specificity desired.

subScores.label: Market & Why-Now
subScores.rationale: No specific vertical focus; market size hint not provided. Why-now driver is plausible but not strongly evidenced in the source. Competitors are well-known, but wedge is unclear.

subScores.label: Traction / Freshness
subScores.rationale: Only signal is a 2019 funding round; no recent traction (paying customers, active usage, launches) provided. Freshness is poor, resulting in a low score.

scoreRationale: SoundHound shows strong team technical depth but lacks documented prior exits and a specific vertical focus. Defensibility and product are moderate, while market specificity and recent traction are weak. The overall weighted score is below the investment threshold given the thesis emphasis on vertical focus and fresh traction.
